claim.why_it_matters: Same convention gap as 11.6.2: the fenced figure drops the printed underlining and carries no Figure notes blockquote, so the required/optional status of the reserved words is unrecorded. Here every reserved word in the figure IS underlined, so no legal syntax is made to look illegal - but the transcription's own convention (218 Figure notes elsewhere) is not honoured, and a downstream reader cannot distinguish 'all words required' from 'underlining simply not transcribed'.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. (1) TEXT IS IDENTICAL. I rendered p312 at 300 dpi and compared it against specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 13623-13627. The printed 12.2.1 general format reads 'ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.' / '[ configuration-section ]' / '[ input-output-section ]'; the fence contains exactly those three lines, same order, same brackets, same trailing period. Nothing is missing, added, reflowed, or altered. The claim's own two quotations differ in no character - only in typographic underlining. (2) GLYPH INSPECTION. Cropping the figure region (250,1040)-(1000,1300) and upscaling 3x, I see one continuous rule beneath E-N-V-I-R-O-N-M-E-N-T, a clear gap, then a second rule beneath D-I-V-I-S-I-O-N; the trailing period sits outside the second rule. So the claim's description of the printed page is accurate. But per the transcription's own 5.2.2 (line 2628) underlined uppercase = keyword = required, and 5.2.3 (line 2641) non-underlined uppercase = optional word. EVERY uppercase word in this figure is underlined, so there is no required/optional distinction present for the underlining to encode. A reader deriving grammar from the plain fence writes 'ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.' - character-for-character what the underlined figure mandates. Meaning is not changed. The claim concedes this itself ('no legal syntax is made to look illegal'). (3) THE 'MISSING' FIGURE NOTES ARE NOT PDF CONTENT. The PDF contains no 'Figure notes' paragraph anywhere; it is a transcriber-added annotation layer. Its absence cannot be a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. (4) THE CLAIMED CONVENTION IS NOT UNIVERSAL, SO THIS IS NOT A DEVIATION. Measured over the whole 53,201-line transcription: 510 fenced blocks exist; only 214 are followed by a Figure notes blockquote. 296 fences - the MAJORITY, 58% - lack one, exactly like p312. And ZERO of the 510 fences contain <u> markup anywhere in the document (all 156 <u> tags across 97 lines sit OUTSIDE fences, in the alternate non-fenced format style). 'No <u> inside the fence' is therefore a document-wide invariant, not a p312 defect; the claim's framing of '218 Figure notes elsewhere' implies a near-universal practice that the measurement contradicts. (5) SIBLING CHECK. The directly comparable division-structure formats get identical treatment: 11.2.1 Identification division structure (line 12769) is a plain fence with no underlining and no Figure notes, as is 11.6.2 (line 12973). p312 is consistent with its own siblings. Faulting it would require faulting several hundred fences. Verdict: no content discrepancy; the residual difference is pure formatting plus incomplete coverage of an editorial annotation layer that has no counterpart in the source PDF.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-312 figure error. The 12.2.1 general format is transcribed character-for-character correctly (3 lines, exact text, exact brackets and period). The printed page does underline ENVIRONMENT and DIVISION as two separate rules with the period excluded - confirmed by direct glyph inspection - but since all uppercase words in this figure are keywords, dropping the underlining removes no required/optional information and changes no derivable syntax. What genuinely exists is a repository-wide transcription-quality observation, not a per-page discrepancy: the transcription renders general formats in two inconsistent styles - fenced plain-text blocks (510 of them, 0 carrying <u>, only 214 annotated with a Figure notes blockquote) versus non-fenced lines that DO carry <u> markup (156 tags). If the Figure notes annotation program is to be completed, it should be tracked once as a global coverage task over the ~296 un-annotated fences, and prioritized toward figures where underlining IS load-bearing (i.e. figures mixing underlined and non-underlined uppercase words, such as 'data-name-1 IS [ <u>NOT</u> ] <u>OMITTED</u>' at line 9984 where the non-underlined IS is optional). Page 312 is not such a figure and should not be ledgered as structural.
